is_anopheles.evidence: Studies Anopheles gambiae s.l. (molecular M form) and Anopheles funestus (e.g. Title, Abstract, page 1).

reports_target_markers.evidence: Tested for knockdown resistance (kdr) using PCR with primers Agd1, Agd2, Agd3, Agd4 citing Fanello et al. 2003, which assays Vgsc L995F (L1014F) (page 3, 'Molecular forms and kdr analysis').

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Page 4, 'Molecular forms and kdr': 'The kdr PCR assay of 192 of the samples (148 survivors (DDT: 67; deltamethrin: 17; permethrin: 64: and 44 susceptible ones) however, did not reveal any kdr mutations in the mosquitoes.' Thus N=192 (100% SS / 0% R alleles).

african_field_population.evidence: F1 progeny from wild indoor resting blood-fed and gravid females collected across ecological zones in Kassena-Nankana District, northern Ghana (page 2, 'Field procedures').

is_primary_study.evidence: Primary empirical field bioassay and resistance surveillance study.

sub_country_location.evidence: Kassena-Nankana District, Upper East Region, northern Ghana (10°30' to 11°00'N, 1°00' to 1°30'W) (page 2).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Mosquitoes collected between November 2006 and October 2007 (page 4, 'Discussion').

duplicate_risk.evidence: Routine field collections conducted specifically for this study by Navrongo Health Research Centre.

supplement.evidence: All relevant bioassay data, sample sizes, and genotyping outcomes are described completely within the text and tables of the main manuscript.

assessment.summary: This study tested pyrethroid and DDT susceptibility in F1 progeny of Anopheles gambiae and Anopheles funestus collected in 2006–2007 from Kassena-Nankana District, northern Ghana. A subsample of 192 An. gambiae (148 bioassay survivors and 44 susceptible individuals; all identified as M molecular form) were genotyped for the kdr mutation (Vgsc L995F) using PCR, with 0% mutant alleles detected (all 192 were homozygous susceptible).
